summary: Operators can attach free-form tags to alerts, remove them, see them in AlertResponse, and filter GET /api/alerts by tag.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new Tag entity has a many-to-many relationship with Alert, backed by a new join table and EF migration.
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags adds one or more tags to the alert, deduplicating case-insensitively.
An alert holds at most 10 tags and each tag is 1-30 characters; violations are rejected with 400.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes the tag from the alert; it returns 404 if the alert or the tag assignment does not exist.
GET /api/alerts accepts an optional tag filter that composes with isActive, severity, date range, and search.

implementation_steps: 1. Add Tag.cs and the Tags collection on Alert.cs in AlertService.Models.
2. Add tag limit constants to AlertConstants.cs.
3. Add AddAlertTagsRequest.cs, the Tag filter in AlertQueryRequest.cs, and Tags in AlertResponse.cs.
5. Extend IAlertRepository.cs with the tag filter (before cancellationToken), AddTagsAsync, and RemoveTagAsync.
6. Add DbSet<Tag> in AlertDbContext.cs and create TagConfiguration.cs.
7. Update AlertRepository.cs to include Tags, filter by tag, and implement AddTagsAsync and RemoveTagAsync.
8. Create the AddAlertTags migration, its Designer, and update AlertDbContextModelSnapshot.cs.
10. Add AddAlertTagsResult.cs and extend IAlertService.cs and AlertManagementService.cs.
11. Add the POST and DELETE tag endpoints to AlertsController.cs.
12. Run the build command and fix compile errors only.

planned_tests.test: Alert with tags persists and reloads through the Tag many-to-many join.
AddTagsAsync stores new tags and reuses an existing Tag row shared by two alerts.
Service dedupes tags case-insensitively within the request and against tags already on the alert.
AddTagsAsync service returns a null alert when the alert id does not exist.
Controller POST returns the updated alert for valid tags and 404 when the alert is missing.
Service flags TagLimitExceeded when existing plus new tags exceed 10, and controller returns 400.
Exactly 10 tags is accepted; request tags of length 0, 31, and whitespace-only fail validation; 30 chars passes.
RemoveTagAsync removes the assignment case-insensitively and controller returns 204.
Controller returns 404 when the alert is missing or the tag is not assigned.
GetAllAsync with a tag returns only alerts that have it, case-insensitively.
Tag filter combined with isActive, severity, date range, and search narrows results; service passes the tag to the repository.
ToResponse maps tags as a name-sorted list, empty when the alert has none.

contract_changes.api: New POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags and DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag}; GET /api/alerts gains optional tag query parameter; AlertResponse gains tags array.
contract_changes.database: New Tags and AlertTags tables, unique IX_Tags_Name, new migration AddAlertTags.

boundaries.primary_slice: Alert tagging across AlertService.API controller/service, DTO, Models, Data, and Data.SQL.
out_of_scope: Tag management endpoints (list, rename, delete tags)
Tag sorting or tag counts in the summary endpoint

assumptions: Tags are trimmed; uniqueness and matching are case-insensitive for add, remove, and filter.
Re-adding a tag already on the alert is a no-op, not an error.
A request that would push an alert past 10 tags is rejected whole with 400, and nothing is added.
The tag filter is an exact case-insensitive match on one tag name.
Migration files are hand-authored to match EF output because dotnet ef cannot be run in this stage.
Tag rows are not deleted when their last alert assignment is removed.
risks: Medium: schema migration plus Include on the list query; rollback = revert the commit and apply the Down migration.
Low: two concurrent requests creating the same new tag can hit the unique index and return 500.
Low: positional GetAllAsync callers could mis-bind if tag is not placed last before cancellationToken.
scope_override_reason: Many-to-many tagging crosses 7 projects and needs a migration, Designer, snapshot, and SQL script, so 20 source files are needed; 5 test files cover it after the review R5 split and R4 coverlet addition.

Q2: tag casing stored → lowercased (trimmed, lowercase invariant)
